reconcile.note: Gill separates the eternal heaven of heavens in Genesis 1:1 from the visible firmament later named Heaven, so the New Testament describes further preparation, not a rival origin.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Thomas Paine faults Genesis for piling up heavens, firmament, and days in a sequence he reads as internally confused rather than a coherent account of when heaven began.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason (1794).

sides.snippet: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
sides.verseText: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

sides.snippet: In my Father's house are many mansions. If it weren't so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you.
